RotatingLog.write throws on any open/rename failure (EACCES, ENOSPC, a failed rotate), and a throw inside an EventEmitter listener emitted from the stream's afterWrite tick is an uncaughtException: the daemon dies with exit 1 on the first request after its log becomes unwritable, without an answer, without a drain and without its stopping event. This contradicts the shell's own contract at http.ts:333 ('No throw inside handle, the log's included, may ... end the daemon') and the care taken at http.ts:336-340, 371, 393, 401 to make every other log write non-fatal. Reproduced: a scratch script started the service on a temp home, chmod 0400 the service.jsonl, sent GET /.well-known/fabric-service; the process exited 1 with 'EACCES ... at RotatingLog.write ... at ServerResponse.<anonymous> (http.ts:288)' before the first answer was read.; check: pnpm -s exec vitest run apps/agent/src/service -t 'log cannot be written' passes with a test that chmods servicePaths(dirs).serviceLog to 0400 after start, calls /.well-known/fabric-service twice and gets 200 both times, then close() resolves; the existing suite stays 99+ green.
